news.2026-10-31-france-pib-recule-t3.tit: France contracts in the third quarter while the eurozone holds up
news.2026-10-31-france-pib-recule-t3.sum: French GDP shrinks by 0.1% between July and September, while the eurozone grows by 0.4%.
news.2026-10-31-france-pib-recule-t3.poi: Insee estimates that the French economy shrank by 0.1% in the third quarter, whereas economists expected a slight increase [1][2][3].
Foreign trade weighs the most (exports down 1.7%), while household consumption rises by 0.4% [2].
Meanwhile, the eurozone grows by 0.4% (versus 0.6% the previous quarter) and Germany by 0.2% [3][4].
news.2026-10-31-france-pib-recule-t3.why: Key takeaway: France is lagging behind its neighbors just as it has to vote on a tight budget [1][3].
A falling GDP means less wealth produced, and therefore less revenue for the state, while the deficit is already high. This is only a first estimate: Insee will revise it [2].
news.2026-10-31-france-pib-recule-t3.for: A stalling economy weighs on jobs and on the budget's room for maneuver: it is one more argument in the debates on taxes and spending in the coming weeks [1][3].
news.2026-10-31-france-couvre-feu-paris-: The curfew hours for minors differ between sources: the police prefecture's order is the authoritative text.
Paris: curfews over the All Saints' Day weekend after the October looting
The police prefecture bans nighttime movement for minors, then for everyone, in certain neighborhoods from October 30 to November 2.

A curfew targets unaccompanied minors in several areas of Paris, from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m., from Friday evening until Monday morning, November 2 [1][2]. A first order had been suspended by the administrative court, and a new measure followed [1][2].
A second order bans movement for everyone, from 11 p.m. to 6 a.m., in the République and Châtelet-Les Halles areas, from October 31 to November 2 [2][3].
The prefecture cites the looting and damage of October 17 and 18 and the incidents of October 24 (142 arrests) [3].
Key takeaway: this is a rare measure in the capital, taken after several weeks of tension [2][3].
The Prime Minister had asked prefects for "partial" and "localized" curfews [1]. New appeals may still be brought before the courts [2].
If you are in Paris this weekend, check the affected streets on the police prefecture's website before going out late [2][3].
general curfew at République and Les Halles
news.2026-10-31-pologne-cour-constitutio: Poland: the president turns his plane around mid-flight to defend the head of the Constitutional Court
The government has the Court's president suspended, while the head of state refuses to recognize him as removed.
The president of the Constitutional Court, Bogdan Święczkowski, was suspended on Friday evening by judges close to the government, who accuse him of repeatedly breaking the law [1][2].
The Court responds that he remains its president; he and his deputy were denied entry to the building [1][2].
President Karol Nawrocki, who was heading to Senegal, had his plane turn back, went to the Court, helped the judge get in and denounced an attack on the constitutional order [2][3].
Key takeaway: two Polish branches of power are fighting over who runs the country's highest court, and the street is getting involved [2][3].

The government has been trying for weeks to remove judges appointed under the previous government (PiS), while the president has refused to swear in five of the eight new judges [3]. The sources do not settle the question of whether the suspension is legal.
Poland is a heavyweight neighbor in the European Union: a showdown over the rule of law can complicate decisions made by the 27 [2][3].
new judges not sworn in by the president
news.2026-10-31-georgie-azerbaidjan-comm: The content of the signed final document does not yet appear in the sources consulted.
Azerbaijan's Prime Minister in Georgia: transport and energy on the South Caucasus agenda
Ali Asadov spent two days in Georgia for the two countries' joint economic commission.
Azerbaijani Prime Minister Ali Asadov arrived in Tbilisi on October 29 for a two-day working visit [1][3].
He held a one-on-one meeting with his Georgian counterpart Irakli Kobakhidze on October 30 in Sighnaghi, in the Kakheti region [2][4].
The agenda covered the economy, trade, transport, energy and logistics, with the 11th intergovernmental commission and a final document expected [1][3].
Key takeaway: the meeting deals with very concrete topics (transport, energy, logistics) between two South Caucasus neighbors [1][3].
The commission's final text will say which projects move forward first; it is not yet detailed in the sources [1][3].
Transport and energy agreements in the South Caucasus concern the freight routes between Asia and Europe [1][3].
news.2026-10-31-kirghizistan-reseau-elec: Sadyr Japarov's decision on mining licenses is relayed mainly by Eurasianet: to be confirmed with the Kyrgyz government.
Central Asia: winter threatens Soviet-era power grids, Kyrgyzstan freezes crypto mining
The Kyrgyz president will grant no more mining licenses until electricity production has increased.

Eurasianet describes a fragile Central Asian grid, often overloaded according to a study by the Eurasian Development Bank: the problem has less to do with total capacity than with when electricity is available [1].
Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov announced that no new licenses would be granted to power-hungry cryptocurrency mining farms until production increases [1].
In Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, the authorities are betting on energy savings, shutting down mining farms and more imports; Tajikistan exports electricity in summer but sells less of it in winter [2].
Key takeaway: a large share of the power plants and lines dates from the Soviet era, and winter is when demand soars [3].
The World Bank estimates that the region's electricity demand could triple by 2050 if the trend continues [3].
Far from home, but useful to know: cryptocurrencies consume real electricity, and entire countries sometimes have to choose between them and heating [1][2].
possible electricity demand by 2050 in Central Asia
news.2026-10-31-bhoutan-thailande-visite: Bhutan receives a Thai Prime Minister for the first time in eight years
Anutin Charnvirakul signs three agreements in the Himalayan kingdom: health, green agricultural finance and solar energy.
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul is on an official visit to Bhutan from October 30 to November 1, the first by a Thai head of government in eight years [1][3].
Thailand and Bhutan signed three agreements: health, "green" agricultural financing and technical assistance for a 100 MW solar project [2].
The two countries also want to build on their free trade agreement to increase trade and investment [1][2].
Key takeaway: Bhutan, a small kingdom squeezed between India and China, is diversifying its partners, and Thailand gains an unusual ally there [1][3].
The visit coincides with the 37th anniversary of diplomatic relations and with an important event in Gelephu on November 1 [1].
A little-known small country is opening up to solar energy and green agriculture: South and Southeast Asia are forging ties without going through the great powers [1][2].
since the last official visit by a Thai Prime Minister
news.2026-10-31-inde-conteneurs-fabrique: India wants to make its own shipping containers: ten times more within a few years
The government releases 10,000 crore rupees to produce containers that are imported today.
The Indian government has approved a 10,000-crore-rupee plan (the "Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme") to manufacture containers in the country [1][2].
The goal is to go from about 70,000 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEU) per year to 750,000 [1].
The plan runs from 2027-28 to 2039-40: three years to build the factories, then ten years of production support; each new factory must produce at least 100,000 TEU per year [1][2].
Key takeaway: India is seeking to stop depending on foreign suppliers for a basic link in global trade, the container [1][3].
The measure had been announced in the 2026-27 budget; the largest share (8,891 crore) goes to helping factories produce [1][3].
Almost everything you buy has traveled in a container: who makes them, and at what price, affects the cost of sea freight [1][3].
news.2026-10-31-vietnam-banques-etat-65-: Vietnam wants to keep its largest banks under state control
The government sets a floor of 65% public ownership in the large state-owned banks by 2030.
Vietnam has approved a plan setting the state's stake in the large state-owned banks at no less than 65% by 2030 [1][2][3].
The state currently holds about 76.7% of BIDV, 74.8% of Vietcombank and 64.5% of VietinBank, which therefore still has to rise a little [4].
Agribank, for its part, remains 100% state-owned until 2030; the text does not say how the targets will be met [4].
Key takeaway: while many countries sell stakes in their banks, Hanoi chooses to keep control over credit in the economy [1][2].
Controlling the banks makes it possible to steer loans toward sectors deemed strategic, but limits the room for private investors [1][2].
Vietnam has become a workshop of the world for electronics and textiles: how it finances its factories indirectly affects the products you buy [1][2].
minimum state stake in the large banks by 2030
news.2026-10-31-cambodge-tourisme-chute-: Cambodia: almost half as many foreign tourists as a year ago
2.46 million visitors between January and September, versus 4.38 million a year earlier.
Cambodia received 2,464,033 foreign tourists from January to September 2026, versus 4,377,466 in the same period of 2025, a drop of 43.7% [1][2].
Vietnamese (−28%, 651,486) and Chinese (−27.6%, 643,314) remain the top visitors but are declining sharply; Americans are down 5.6% [1].
The Tourism Minister cites bad publicity linked to online scam networks, friction at the border with Thailand and higher fuel prices due to conflicts in the Middle East [1][2].
Key takeaway: tourism is a pillar of the Cambodian economy, and this shock hits hotels, guides and businesses around Angkor [1][2].
The sources do not measure how much each cause contributes to the decline [1][2].
Fuel prices tied to the war around Hormuz are passing through even to travel in Southeast Asia, and therefore to the destinations you can consider [1][2].
news.2026-10-31-ormuz-petroliers-mines-i: The exact Brent level differs between sources (over $117 for CNBC, $112 for Trading Economics) and the mines are an Iranian claim denied by the US military.
Hormuz: Iran claims three oil tankers hit mines, Washington denies it
Attacks on ships have never been as numerous as in October, and oil flows are falling.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim that three oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; the US military denies it, saying the main routes have been cleared of mines [1][2].
According to CNBC, more ships, mostly tankers, were attacked in October than at any other time in the war, and crude rose more than 13% over the month [1].
Crude exports through Hormuz averaged nearly 11.1 million barrels per day in October, but only 7.3 million in the week ending Wednesday, more than 40% below the pre-war level according to Kpler [1].
Key takeaway: even under attack, tankers keep passing through, but in smaller numbers, and the market is paying for it [1].
Brent exceeded $117 according to CNBC, very close to its wartime record ($118.35 in March); another reading gives $112 [1][3].
Expensive oil is paid for at the pump and on the heating bill: the tension in Hormuz directly affects your budget [1][3].
barrels/day through Hormuz, more than 40% below pre-war

news.2026-10-31-venezuela-machado-retour: The date of María Corina Machado's return differs between sources (October 25 or 29); the share of reserves covered by the oil deal comes from Al Jazeera alone.
Venezuela: opposition leader Machado returns from exile and demands elections, criticizing the oil deal with the United States
After about ten months abroad, she calls for a vote in 2027 and more transparency on oil.
María Corina Machado has returned to Caracas after about ten months in exile and is demanding elections; she thanked Donald Trump for his support [1][2].
She criticizes the oil deal signed by interim leader Delcy Rodríguez, which would give up about 20% of the country's reserves, according to Al Jazeera, and calls it opaque [1].
Donald Trump marked the first delivery of Venezuelan oil to Corpus Christi (Texas) a few days after her return; Delcy Rodríguez promises elections without a date [1][3].
Key takeaway: Venezuela is led by the deputy of Maduro, who was captured by the United States in January, and its oil is now heading to Texas [1][2].
The question is when Venezuelans will vote, and who will benefit from the oil [1][3].
More Venezuelan oil on the market may help calm energy prices, but the deal raises questions about democracy and transparency [1][3].

news.2026-10-31-perou-fujimori-prison-sa: Peru wants to copy El Salvador's mega-prison: Keiko Fujimori visits the CECOT
The Peruvian president announces two new prisons, one of them modeled on the Salvadoran one.
Peru's president Keiko Fujimori visited the CECOT on Thursday, October 29, the maximum-security prison built by Nayib Bukele in El Salvador [1][2].
She announced that Peru would build two new prisons, one inspired by the CECOT and the other with lower security, without giving a cost or a date [3].
Bukele said El Salvador would share its experience so that Peru can adapt it to its laws [3].
Key takeaway: the "Bukele model" is increasingly appealing to Latin American leaders facing crime [1][2].
The CECOT became famous when the Trump administration sent more than 250 deported Venezuelans there, accused of gang ties, with no evidence presented [1].
Security has become a major electoral theme in the region, and the choices made in Lima or San Salvador influence debates elsewhere [1][2].
Venezuelans sent to the CECOT by Washington
news.2026-10-31-nigeria-dangote-raffiner: The amounts come from anonymous sources cited by Reuters; the allocation and the stock market listing are not yet official.
Nigeria: the Dangote refinery's stock market debut draws about three times the targeted amount
Orders reportedly reach 6.4 trillion naira, or nearly $4.8 billion.
According to available information, the Dangote refinery's share offering was heavily oversubscribed at its close on October 27 [1][2].
According to Reuters, citing two sources, orders reach about 6.4 trillion naira ($4.78 billion), nearly three times the target of 2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) [1].
The price is 525 naira per share; an option could bring the operation to more than $2.1 billion, and small retail investors would be served first [1][2].
Key takeaway: this IPO would be one of the largest in Africa, driven by investors' appetite for local refining [1][2].
Investors might receive only part of the shares they requested; the allocation and the listing on the Lagos stock exchange are still to come [1][2].
A giant African refiner reduces the continent's dependence on imported fuel, which matters when oil is expensive [1][2].
demand relative to the offering target
news.2026-10-31-afrique-raffineries-or-e: A single source (QNC News): Ethiopian and Zambian figures to be confirmed with the governments.
Africa: Ethiopia and Zambia open gold refineries to keep value at home
Four African countries are launching or expanding gold refineries in 2026, while the metal remains very expensive.
Ethiopia launched a $50 million precious metals refinery in October, with a capacity of more than 600 tonnes per year; the state holds a majority stake [1].
Zambia unveiled on October 25 in Lusaka a refinery capable of reaching 99 to 99.99% purity, with a two-year plan to regulate artisanal gold mining [1].
Gold exports earned Ethiopia $5.6 billion in 2025-2026, and Zambia has issued 1,201 artisanal gold mining licenses since 2023 [1].
Key takeaway: refining locally earns more than selling raw gold, and limits smuggling [1].
African countries increasingly seek to process their resources locally rather than export them raw [1].
Gold serves as a safe haven and goes into electronics: where it is refined changes who captures the wealth in the chain [1].
